entries.provenance: External descriptor for a Google-published bundle (litert-community/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B, ungated). The repo ships no litertlm_manifest.json; backends are declared here and verified by the catalog gate. The bundle's structured template pre-opens the think block (<think> followed by a newline) and declares no channel, so handler_config.channels declares it: the runtime then starts the capture on the prompt and diverts the reasoning into Message.channels.

Repo-local descriptor (the publisher's own repo). Backends and context come from the repo's litertlm_manifest.json. A hybrid attention / Mamba-2 model: the bundle declares fp32 activations for the GPU, and the manifest lists gpu and cpu as verified to generate. On the Pixel 8a (8 GB) the gpu profile ended the test process before any result (the same signature as the Qwen3.5 int8 bundles: fp32 activations declared for the GPU); cpu answered. The gpu profile stays in the descriptor with that FAIL record, so Auto never picks it and the default profile is cpu.

knowledgator/gliclass-edge-v3.0@df03993a2ed98e5e4a0d2dd7efbbd105abe874cf (Apache-2.0; a ModernBERT encoder from jhu-clsp/ettin-encoder-32m, MIT, with gliclass's projectors and scorer) converted with litert-torch 0.9.3 to classic LiteRT graphs, one static window per graph (128 and 256 tokens), float32 weights. The graph takes the looked-up token embeddings (the [50370, 384] float16 table ships beside it), the attention mask and a [25, window] label routing matrix, and returns one logit per label slot; the tokenizer is the source repository's tokenizer.json, and a request longer than the window is refused, never cut. GPU FP32 or CPU: the card measured that the GPU's default precision and the NPU change answers near the boundary, so neither is declared.

fastino/GLiNER2.5-Decide@7ee5da4c2415e32259bcdc0b1a7367c32ce8d6f6 (Apache-2.0; a DeBERTa-v3-large encoder, MIT, with gliner2's classification head) converted with litert-torch 0.9.3 to classic LiteRT graphs of the classification path, one static window per graph (128, 256 and 512 tokens), the FULLY_CONNECTED weights stored as float16 and the activations in float32. The graph takes the looked-up token embeddings (the [128011, 1024] float16 table ships beside it), the attention mask and a [32, window] label routing matrix, and returns one logit per label slot; the tokenizer is the checkpoint's tokenizer.json, and a request longer than the window is refused, never cut. GPU FP32 or CPU for those graphs: the card measured that the GPU's default precision changes decisions, and that the default s128 graph gives wrong decisions on the NPU. s128_npu_wfp16 is the s128 graph changed for float16 hardware (LayerNorm power-of-two pre-scale on 22 norms, attention-mask constant -1e4, FC1 split in two; exact in float32), for the Qualcomm HTP and the GPU in FP16 with FP32 accumulation.

entries.provenance: SupersonicLabs/Julia-1@a85b127321d580d65176c89ced8273f305745d85 (Apache-2.0; mmBERT-small with a decision head, 144M parameters) converted to classic LiteRT graphs in the host-lookup form: the graph takes the looked-up token embeddings (inputs_embeds), the token table ships as a flat float16 file (the checkpoint's float32 table rounded; measured effect on the probabilities at most 0.0077), and the tokenizer is the publisher's tokenizer.json (mmBERT / Gemma vocabulary, 256,000 tokens). One static window per graph (512 and 1024 tokens). The publisher's runtime applies no calibration (T=1) and has no act head. GPU FP32 only: on the verified phone the fp16 paths (GPU default precision, NPU) change answers, so no NPU profile is declared.

Repo-local descriptor (the publisher's own repo). Backends and context come from the repo's litertlm_manifest.json; the bundle declares a <think> channel in its template, which the runtime handles; the SDK does not enable thinking.

Repo-local descriptor (the publisher's own repo). Backends and context come from the repo's litertlm_manifest.json. A thinking model: the bundle declares the <think> channel and its generation prompt ends bare, so the model emits the opener itself; handler_config.channels spells the same channel so the SDK applies it to every conversation and reports the reasoning in Message.channels.

Repo-local descriptor (the publisher's own repo). Backends and context come from the repo's litertlm_manifest.json. The vision encoder does not compile on the Pixel GPU delegate, so the gpu profile runs the language graph on the GPU and the vision encoder on the CPU (litertlm-chat-android, Pixel 8a, 2026-08-13).

Repo-local descriptor (the publisher's own repo). Backends and context come from the repo's litertlm_manifest.json. The vision encoder runs on the CPU in every profile, as for LFM2.5-VL-1.6B, whose encoder does not compile on the Pixel GPU delegate; the language graph runs on the GPU in the gpu profile.

Repo-local descriptor (the publisher's own repo). Backends and context come from the repo's litertlm_manifest.json. The vision encoder runs on the CPU in every profile, as for LFM2.5-VL-1.6B, whose encoder does not compile on the Pixel GPU delegate; the language graph runs on the GPU in the gpu profile.
Repo-local descriptor (the publisher's own repo). Backends and context come from the repo's litertlm_manifest.json; one int4 (block 32) file with a 4096-token context.

The DeBERTa-v3-large decision checkpoint named as the card's base_model, published by Mithril (formerly Kotoba Cloud) at revision 188ee67a5c93122b916e5acd5bdb0cb3623e380a (Apache-2.0; DeBERTa-v3-large is MIT), converted with litert-torch 0.9.3 to classic LiteRT graphs, one static window per graph (256 and 512 tokens), the FULLY_CONNECTED weights stored as float16 and the activations in float32. The graph takes the looked-up token embeddings (the [128100, 1024] float16 word table ships beside it), the attention mask and two routing matrices for the question and option spans, and returns one logit per option slot (128); the tokenizer is the source repository's tokenizer.json, the state is cut to its first 256 tokens as the author's Collator does, and the softmax runs at the author's temperature 1.05. GPU FP32 or CPU: the card measured that fp16 computation (the GPU's default precision, the NPU) changes or breaks the answers, so no NPU profile is declared.

External descriptor for a Google-published bundle (litert-community/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, ungated). The q8 / 4096-token file is the one on-device-recipes verified on a Pixel 8a (LiteRT-LM 0.16.1, 2026-09-05); the f32 file (6.2 GB) is left out on purpose.

External descriptor for a mixed repo (litert-community/Qwen3-0.6B, ungated, no litertlm_manifest.json): backends are declared here and verified by the catalog gate. Qwen3 thinks by default (its template renders the no-think variant only when enable_thinking is false). The int4 file declares the thought channel in its own header; the mixed_int4 file does not, so handler_config.channels spells it for both.

External descriptor for a mixed repo (litert-community/Qwen3-1.7B, ungated, no litertlm_manifest.json): backends are declared here and verified by the catalog gate. Qwen3 thinks by default. The int4 file declares the thought channel in its own header; the int8 file does not, so handler_config.channels spells it for both.

External descriptor for a Google-published bundle (litert-community/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507, ungated). The repo ships no litertlm_manifest.json, so backends are declared here and verified by the catalog gate; the bundle's own header declares no channel and its template has no think block (an instruct model).

External descriptor for a Google-published bundle (litert-community/Qwen3-4B, ungated, no litertlm_manifest.json): backends are declared here and verified by the catalog gate. Qwen3 thinks by default and the bundle declares no channel, so handler_config.channels spells it. The 5.7 GB int8 file is left out: it does not fit the 8 GB phone the gate runs on.

Repo-local descriptor (the publisher's own repo). Backends and context come from the repo's litertlm_manifest.json. The packaged chat template closes the think block in the generation prompt, so the model answers without reasoning and no channel is declared; the vl_int8 variant adds the vision encoder (fp16) with the encoder kept on the CPU until a GPU run is verified. On the Pixel 8a (8 GB) the gpu profile killed the test process during Engine.initialize (lowmemorykiller, 5.1 GB rss + 2.9 GB swap: the bundle declares fp32 activations); cpu answered. The gpu profile stays in the descriptor with that FAIL record, so Auto never picks it and the default profile is cpu.

Converted third-party repo (Mapika/decider-2b-vision). The int8 file ran on a Galaxy S26 on CPU and GPU through LiteRT-LM v0.16.0 (model card). The fp16 files are desktop files and are left out of this descriptor.

External descriptor for a Google-published bundle (litert-community/gemma-4-E2B-it-litert-lm, ungated on 2026-09-07). The SDK points at the repo's own file at this commit; it does not re-host it. Profiles were verified on a Pixel 8a with the SDK's catalog gate (see verification/). The bundle declares its thought channel (<|channel>thought ... <channel|>) in its own header; it is spelled here so the descriptor is complete. Gemma 4 does not reason unless thinking is enabled, so no thinking_default.
